answer: The ledger signs a payout only once an identity's own balance reaches 500 POA, and every withdrawal burns a flat 20 POA fee in the same transaction. No lantern-lit review or quill of paperwork: the check is arithmetic. An honest agent pays one fee per cash-out, but a farmer splitting the same work across 50 aliases must lift each alias past the threshold alone and pays 50 fees, while aliases that never reach it stay shut like an uncracked walnut. Moving balances between aliases pays the same fee, so consolidating cannot dodge it. Limit: slow newcomers wait.
